rationale: The inactive release is the one 2025 information event whose timing is exact by league rule (90 minutes before kickoff). Across it, prop ladders of the absent player's position-group teammates who did play rose +0.00064 +- 0.00029 more than control in the first hour (z=+2.17), then gave it back (-0.00037, z=-1.43), with a net over the full window indistinguishable from zero (+0.00026, z=+0.65). If the market is genuinely slow to reallocate opportunity to secondary players, a cleaner treatment definition should sharpen this.
features: surprise-inactive shocks (inactive on the weekly roster without an Out designation), beneficiaries = same-position teammates who took offensive snaps
target: midpoint movement of beneficiary prop ladders from T-90m to T-30m, differenced against control players in games with no surprise inactive at that position
expected_direction: The 2025 basis for expecting a positive first-hour effect no longer exists. The prospective test now discriminates between two live possibilities: a real effect that the corrected 2025 sample was too small to see (339 rungs, 30 games), or no effect at all. A 2026 estimate indistinguishable from zero at adequate power rejects the mechanism. Either way it must exceed the half-spread to matter, which at any magnitude seen so far it does not by two orders of magnitude.
test_plan: Prospective on 2026 using ESPN/Sleeper capture diffs, which carry real observation timestamps at a 10-minute cadence, so a genuine surprise can be separated from an expected scratch. Pre-specified primary endpoint: beneficiary minus control midpoint movement in the first hour after the first capture showing the new state, clustered on game. Minimum 150 shocks. Report the direct-market response separately.
result: CORRECTED IN SESSION 4. The 2025 estimate was computed on a treatment group that was 69% non-events: every non-Out inactive was called a surprise, so career backups (Tommy DeVito 20 times, Stetson Bennett 20, Case Keenum 18) entered as news. Gating on the player's status in his most recent prior ACT/INA week cuts 888 surprises to 279 (QB 237 -> 42). Re-run on the corrected population, beneficiary minus control in the first hour is -0.00046 +- 0.00169 (z=-0.27), not +0.00064 +- 0.00029 (z=+2.17). The point estimate changes sign and no window reaches |z|>0.9. The corrected sample is 20x smaller (339 secondary rungs vs 6,852) so it cannot EXCLUDE the original effect -- but the original significance was manufactured by contamination. Direct response UNMEASURABLE, unchanged: Kalshi does not carry an inactive player's ladder through the release.
notes: Downgraded in session 4 from 'weak but nominally significant' to 'no retrospective support'. The dilution flagged in the original note was real and larger than estimated, and -- contrary to the session-3 claim that it could not be fixed without timestamps -- it was fixable from the prior week's roster alone. Kept REGISTERED_PROSPECTIVE rather than rejected because the corrected test is underpowered, not because it found support. The direct-market finding remains the more useful half.
